sourcedFrom: MPA DEFENDER SERIES — OWNER'S MANUAL (MPA5700DMG Carbine, MPA57DMG Pistol) — 57DMG / 5700DMG — read from the document's own cover (ABSENT)
cleanIntro: The Defender 5.7 is MPA's 5.7x28mm blowback, and it comes apart on two receiver pins like its 9mm and .45 siblings — with one real difference at the bolt. On this gun the bolt assembly simply slides back and OUT of the rear of the upper receiver. There is no cocking-handle lift and no alignment hole; if you have read the 10/30 manual and are looking for them, they are not on this rifle. The hammer still drops when the upper comes off, and it still has to be re-cocked by hand before the upper goes back.

steps.title: ⛔ Safety to SAFE, magazine out, then assume the chamber is loaded
steps.action: Treat the gun as loaded. Turn the safety selector to Safe, press the magazine catch down with your thumb and pull the magazine clear. Then assume there is still a round in the chamber, run the bolt back to eject it, and LOOK to confirm the chamber is empty.
steps.prose: MPA writes the assumption into the procedure rather than leaving it to judgement, which is the right way round.
steps.aside: After magazine has been removed from weapon, assume that there is still a round in the chamber.
steps.quote: Always treat the gun as if it is loaded. Turn the safety selector to the “Safe” position. Press the Mag Catch downward with your thumb and pull on the magazine. This should allow the magazine to be completely removed.
steps.cite: MPA DEFENDER SERIES — OWNER'S MANUAL (MPA5700DMG Carbine, MPA57DMG Pistol) — 57DMG / 5700DMG — read from the document's own cover — Unloading, printed p.7

steps.title: ⚠ 5.7x28mm carries a long way — know what is downrange
steps.action: MPA flags the cartridge specifically: 5.7x28mm is high-powered, has tremendous range and can travel well over a mile. That matters for where the muzzle points during the strip as much as on the range.
steps.prose: A small round is not a short-range one. The manual says so about this gun in particular.
steps.quote: The MPA57DMG and MPA5700DMG utilize a high powered cartridge – 5.7x28mm. This round has a tremendous range and can travel well over a mile in distance.
steps.cite: MPA DEFENDER SERIES — OWNER'S MANUAL (MPA5700DMG Carbine, MPA57DMG Pistol) — 57DMG / 5700DMG — read from the document's own cover — Firing the weapon, printed p.7

steps.title: Both receiver pins out, then lift the FRONT of the upper
steps.action: With the gun proved empty and the hammer released, drive out the inner receiver pin and then the outer one and remove both by hand. The upper advances slightly forward; lift its FRONT and draw the upper and bolt assembly out of the frame. The hammer releases as it comes — MPA says this is normal.
steps.prose: Remember the hammer falling. It is the thing you have to undo before this goes back together.
steps.quote: Once the receiver pins have been removed, the upper receiver will advance forward slightly. Lift the front of the upper receiver up as shown below. You will hear the hammer release (this is normal).
steps.cite: MPA DEFENDER SERIES — OWNER'S MANUAL (MPA5700DMG Carbine, MPA57DMG Pistol) — 57DMG / 5700DMG — read from the document's own cover — Cleaning and maintenance, printed p.8

steps.title: ⛔ Bolt slides STRAIGHT OUT THE BACK — no cocking-handle lift on this gun
steps.action: Slide the bolt assembly all the way back until it comes out of the rear of the upper receiver. That is the whole step. The 9mm and .45 Defenders need the cocking handle lifted at an alignment hole first; this one does not, and looking for that hole on a 5.7 is looking for something that is not there.
steps.prose: The single place the two Defender manuals diverge, and the reason this gun has its own guide.
steps.quote: Slide bolt assembly all the back until it comes out the back of the upper receiver
steps.cite: MPA DEFENDER SERIES — OWNER'S MANUAL (MPA5700DMG Carbine, MPA57DMG Pistol) — 57DMG / 5700DMG — read from the document's own cover — Cleaning and maintenance, printed p.8

steps.title: Field strip complete — clean it and wipe with LIGHT gun oil
steps.action: Frame, upper receiver, bolt assembly and two receiver pins. Clean the residue off every part and wipe with a light gun oil — MPA's words. Keep the two pins together and keep them straight; the inner and outer pins are different parts.
steps.prose: Four pieces and two pins. Light oil, not a coating.
steps.quote: Clean any residue from all parts and wipe with a light gun oil.
steps.cite: MPA DEFENDER SERIES — OWNER'S MANUAL (MPA5700DMG Carbine, MPA57DMG Pistol) — 57DMG / 5700DMG — read from the document's own cover — Cleaning and maintenance, printed p.8

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The hammer must be re-cocked by hand, exactly as on the 9mm guns
deepSteps.action: Removing the upper drops the hammer forward. Before the upper goes back on, rotate the hammer up and back toward the rear of the frame and then down until it clicks and is held by the sear. The upper will not seat properly otherwise.
deepSteps.prose: The one thing both Defender manuals agree on completely.
deepSteps.aside: Reinstall the bolt assembly in the opposite direction as it came out.
deepSteps.quote: After removing the upper receiver the hammer will not be cocked. It will be pivoted forward. Before reinstalling the upper receiver the hammer must be cocked. Rotate hammer up and back toward the back of frame, then down until it clicks and is held back by the sear. The hammer is now cocked.
deepSteps.cite: MPA DEFENDER SERIES — OWNER'S MANUAL (MPA5700DMG Carbine, MPA57DMG Pistol) — 57DMG / 5700DMG — read from the document's own cover — Cleaning and maintenance, printed p.8

deepSteps.title: Light gun oil — the tolerances are the reason
deepSteps.action: Clean the residue off and wipe with a LIGHT gun oil. These are close-tolerance blowback guns; a heavy film collects the next lot of fouling and changes how the bolt runs.
deepSteps.prose: Light is a specification here, not a figure of speech.
deepSteps.quote: Clean any residue from all parts and wipe with a light gun oil.
deepSteps.cite: MPA DEFENDER SERIES — OWNER'S MANUAL (MPA5700DMG Carbine, MPA57DMG Pistol) — 57DMG / 5700DMG — read from the document's own cover — Cleaning and maintenance, printed p.8

deepSteps.title: ⚠ The parts list says 9mm; the gun is 5.7
deepSteps.action: MPA's parts list in this book labels the bolt and recoil components "9mm" — part numbering carried over from the 9mm Defenders. The book is the 5.7 book and the text is explicit that these guns use 5.7x28mm. Order parts by the PART NUMBER, not by the caliber word beside it.
deepSteps.prose: A labelling quirk worth knowing before you phone a supplier and describe the wrong gun.
deepSteps.quote: The MPA57DMG and MPA5700DMG utilize a high powered cartridge – 5.7x28mm. This round has a tremendous range and can travel well over a mile in distance.
deepSteps.cite: MPA DEFENDER SERIES — OWNER'S MANUAL (MPA5700DMG Carbine, MPA57DMG Pistol) — 57DMG / 5700DMG — read from the document's own cover — Firing the weapon, printed p.7

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHAMBER
tasks: Brush and patch the bore from the chamber end until patches come out clean.
Scrub the chamber; 5.7x28mm is a bottlenecked case and leaves a shoulder ring of fouling a straight-wall pistol round does not.

cleaning.name: BOLT ASSEMBLY
tasks: Clean the bolt face, the extractor and the firing-pin channel.
Wipe the recoil rod and its spring; check the ejector rod is straight and secure.

cleaning.name: UPPER AND FRAME
tasks: Clean the upper receiver's interior and the bolt's travel surfaces.
Wipe the frame, hammer and sear; confirm the hammer pivots freely and is held when cocked by hand.

reassembly: Bolt assembly back into the upper in the opposite direction it came out — straight in at the rear.
⛔ RE-COCK THE HAMMER BY HAND: rotate it up and back toward the rear of the frame, then down until it clicks and the sear holds it.
Upper receiver and bolt assembly back onto the frame, reversing the strip.
Outer pin, then inner pin, seated fully by hand.
⛔ Function-check before the gun goes away.
fncheck: With the gun CLEAR: work the safety selector between Safe and Fire and confirm it indexes positively. Run the bolt fully back and let it go forward under spring pressure alone — it should close without help. Confirm the hammer is cocked and that the trigger releases it cleanly on an empty chamber. Insert an EMPTY magazine, confirm the catch holds it, and confirm it releases cleanly on the thumb.
